name: ctrl-q-qvd-viewer
description: View Qlik Sense and QlikView QVD files from within VS Code

ctrl-q-qvd-viewer.maxPreviewRows.description: Maximum number of rows to load from the QVD file for preview and pagination

enumDescriptions: Tab character (\t) - Good general purpose delimiter
Pipe character (|) - Recommended when data contains commas
Comma (,) - Standard CSV-style, but may conflict with data
Auto-detect - Automatically choose the best delimiter based on data content
ctrl-q-qvd-viewer.qlikInlineDelimiter.description: Default delimiter for Qlik Sense inline load script exports. You can override this during each export.

ctrl-q-qvd-viewer.csvEscapeFormulas.description: In CSV exports, put an apostrophe before text that Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets would run as a formula: text starting with =, @, a tab or a carriage return, or with + or - followed by something other than a number. Numbers such as -5 and +46 70 123 45 67 are left alone. Turn this off if the files are only read by programs, not opened in a spreadsheet.

ctrl-q-qvd-viewer.csvByteOrderMark.description: Start CSV exports with a UTF-8 byte order mark. Excel on Windows needs it to show å, ä, ö and other non-ASCII text correctly. Some other readers, such as Python's csv module, then read it as part of the first column name.

ctrl-q-qvd-viewer.exportTimeZone.markdownDescription: The time zone a QVD's timestamps were read in, offered first when an export to Parquet, Avro, Arrow, SQLite or PostgreSQL asks for it. Those exports ask when the QVD holds timestamps, and write each one as the instant it was. Name an IANA time zone such as `America/Chicago`, `UTC`, an alias such as `US/Central`, or an offset such as `-06:00`. Leave it empty to offer timestamps as wall clocks with no time zone first, as the QVD holds them. Excel and the text formats always write wall clocks.
